record: Study 3 and ranking-study settings, fixed before any category's demand is compared with its interest
fixed_by: Khant Phyo Wai (with Claude); approved by Khant in chat on 2026-10-13

taxonomy.structure: taxonomy v2 nodes as approved 2026-10-13 (19 broad, 86 middle); v3 adds theme values from print subject headings into the same nodes
taxonomy.assignment: main assignment without title-word evidence; title-word assignments only as a flagged backup for a positive-control category with fewer than 50 works

period.study_end: latest complete month with both interest and demand data

interest.wikipedia_measure: weekly sum of user views of the category's concept articles divided by total English Wikipedia user views that week
interest.gdelt_volume_measure: weekly mentions of mapped GKG themes divided by all mentions that week
interest.gdelt_tone_measure: mention-weighted mean of GDELT tone, positive and negative per category-week

shift_definitions.normal_level: median of the previous 26 weeks (not including the current week)
shift_definitions.ratio_to_normal: this week's value divided by the normal level
shift_definitions.rising_week: ratio >= 1.5 and Mann-Kendall trend over the last 8 weeks (including this week) with tau > 0 and one-sided p < 0.10, using the Hamed-Rao variance correction for autocorrelation
shift_definitions.shift_start: first rising week after at least 8 consecutive weeks with ratio < 1.5
shift_definitions.duration_count: consecutive weeks from the start with ratio >= 1.5
shift_definitions.sustained: duration_count >= 4; label assigned in week 4 using no later weeks
shift_definitions.size: peak ratio up to the labelling week (week 4, or the week the shift ends if earlier)
shift_definitions.seasonal_shift: the same category has a shift start within +/-2 weeks of the same calendar week in at least half of the other years with data; analysed separately, excluded from the main analysis
shift_definitions.gdelt_durations: the Wikipedia thresholds above are scaled for GDELT by the ratio of median shift durations (GDELT/Wikipedia) computed from interest data alone, rounded, minimum 2 weeks; the computed values are appended to this record before any demand data are read
shift_definitions.real_time_rule: every label uses only weeks up to the week being judged; whole-course size and duration are secondary and descriptive only

demand.seattle: per category, month and format (audiobook, ebook, print): sum over works of checkouts x theme strength, divided by all checkouts in that format that month
demand.librivox: per category and month: sum over recordings of Internet Archive views x theme strength, divided by all LibriVox views that month
demand.missing_months: May 2024, June 2024 and August 2025 have no digital Seattle rows; they are treated as missing, never as zero
demand.minimum_size: a category is tested in a format only if it has >= 20 works with checkouts in that format and a median of >= 200 weighted checkouts per month in the 24 months before the window

tests.month_zero: the calendar month containing the shift start week; month 0 is in the post period
tests.event_study: counterfactual = OLS on log share with a linear trend and month-of-year effects, fitted on the 24 months ending at month -7; effect = mean of log(actual) - log(predicted) over the effect window; months -6 to -1 shown as a pre-trend check
tests.synthetic_control: donors = categories at the same level with no shift start in months -6 to +6, not sharing a parent node, and sharing <= 10% of their works with the treated category; non-negative weights summing to 1 fitted on log share for months -24 to -3; effect = mean gap over the effect window; p = rank of the post/pre RMSPE ratio among treated + donors, divided by (number of donors + 1)
tests.placebo_years: same category, same calendar months, every other year from 2017 with data and no shift in that window; report the share of placebo effects >= the real effect
tests.pooled_inference: bootstrap clustered by category, 2,000 resamples, seed 20261013
tests.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg q-values across all shift-level synthetic-control p-values; q < 0.10 reported as detected
tests.significance: one-sided p < 0.05 for single shifts (synthetic-control rank)

positive_controls.rule: the controls are run first; no other result is read until they are reported

controls.name: COVID-19
controls.expected: positive demand effect in at least one format

controls.name: George Floyd / Black Lives Matter
controls.expected: positive demand effect in at least one format

controls.name: #MeToo
controls.category: Sexual violence and domestic violence (narrow, rebuilt from print headings)
controls.expected: positive demand effect in at least one format, if the category passes the minimum size

positive_controls.covid_mix_note: for COVID-19 the health-topic rise is expected to be short and the change in the mix of categories longer (Horta Ribeiro et al., 2021); reported descriptively
positive_controls.if_a_control_fails: check data and mappings for errors only; any fix is logged in DEVIATIONS.md with date and reason; thresholds are not tuned on the demand of non-control categories

power.method: inject multiplicative lifts into the demand of donor (placebo) categories for months 0 to +2 after randomly drawn placebo start months, rerun the synthetic control
power.minimum_detectable_effect: smallest size detected in >= 80% of draws

which_shifts_carry_over.outcome: shift-level effect (log lift, months 0 to +2) from the synthetic control
which_shifts_carry_over.model: OLS of effect on log(size), duration class (reference: fading), broad category fixed effects, format, modern (Seattle) vs classic (LibriVox), with a bootstrap clustered by category
which_shifts_carry_over.lag: month of peak gap within 0 to +6

tone.source: GDELT tone only (no historical social text exists)
tone.feature: mean tone over the first 4 weeks of the shift minus the category's 26-week median tone; same for positive and negative
tone.test: added to the carry-over model; compared with placebo tone features from 200 random non-shift 4-week windows of the same category
tone.lag: same weeks as the shift (no other lags tested)
tone.emotions: not tested historically: no historical social text; lexicon emotions (VADER, NRC) only for the live Bluesky sample, descriptive

ranking_study.outcome: next-month Seattle checkouts per work and format
ranking_study.test_months: 2019-01 to the latest complete month; training uses only months whose outcome is known before each cut-off
models: book-theme graph model if time allows
baselines: the work's own recent demand where it exists
metrics: hit rate top 10% vs realised base rate
ranking_study.helps_rule: a family helps only if it beats CatBoost in more than half of test months with a bootstrap interval above zero
ranking_study.cold_start: results reported separately for works with no demand history

thai: settings to be fixed when Thai data exist, before any Thai demand is compared
disclosures: Study 2 (LibriVox theme tests, adaptations) was run before this record and its results are known.

During the taxonomy check on 2026-10-13, monthly Seattle checkouts were viewed descriptively for four categories: race and racism (2020), epidemics and plagues (2020), sexual violence (2017) and climate change (2019). Race and epidemics showed visible rises; sexual violence and climate change did not. No other category's demand was viewed, and no setting here was tuned on them.

The interest-side checkpoint (Wikipedia and GDELT timelines) was started on 2026-10-13 with these same definitions marked provisional; interest data may be used to set the GDELT durations as described.
deviations: any change after this date is recorded in DEVIATIONS.md with date, reason and whether demand data had been seen
